cases.title: What counts as strength?
cases.claim: The cited report defines strength as defeating other people.

evidence.title: The contrast
evidence.text: The report contrasts overcoming others with self-control in anger.

evidence.title: The scope
evidence.text: It describes a virtue; it is not a fitness or mental-health assessment.

cases.correction: Sahih al-Bukhari 6114 praises controlling oneself when angry.
cases.limit: This does not mean every form of physical strength is condemned.
cases.skill: Read the contrast instead of extracting one familiar word.

sources.label: Sahih al-Bukhari 6114
sources.note: Abu Hurayra’s report contrasts physical victory and self-control in anger.

cases.title: Does a hidden defect matter?
cases.claim: The cited report says concealing a defect cannot affect a sale’s blessing.

evidence.title: Truth and disclosure
evidence.text: The report connects truth and disclosure with blessing.

evidence.title: Concealment
evidence.text: It explicitly contrasts this with lying or hiding a fact.

cases.correction: Sahih al-Bukhari 2079 warns about concealment rather than treating it as harmless.
cases.limit: The report is not a complete legal decision on a visitor’s real dispute.
cases.skill: Read both sides of a conditional statement.

sources.label: Sahih al-Bukhari 2079
sources.note: Hakim ibn Hizam’s report addresses buyer and seller truthfulness.

cases.title: A detail beyond a brief cave report
cases.claim: Sahih al-Bukhari 3653 describes a spider spinning a web at the cave.

evidence.title: The reported concern
evidence.text: Abu Bakr describes concern that the pursuers might see them.

evidence.title: The reply
evidence.text: The brief account records reassurance. It does not describe a spider’s web.

cases.correction: This particular report supports concern and reassurance; it does not supply the web detail.
cases.limit: Omission here does not establish the authenticity or inauthenticity of every other narration about the cave.
cases.skill: Check the exact cited report before importing a familiar detail.

sources.label: Sahih al-Bukhari 3653
sources.note: Abu Bakr’s brief report about the cave; previously retrieved in the canonical research set.

cases.title: An exact anniversary from a report?
cases.claim: The cited Night Journey report establishes an exact Gregorian anniversary.

evidence.title: An event report
evidence.text: The account describes the journey and ascent.

evidence.title: A missing calendar claim
evidence.text: It does not supply an exact Gregorian day and month.

cases.correction: The selected report can support an event account without establishing the precise anniversary claimed.
cases.limit: This is a scope finding about the cited report, not a complete survey of all historical date discussions.
cases.skill: Separate evidence for an event from evidence for its date.

sources.label: Sahih al-Bukhari 3887
sources.note: Malik ibn Sasaa’s Night Journey report; previously retrieved for the Seerah source set.

cases.title: A phrase detached from its report
cases.claim: “No blame” in 2:158 means the walk between Safa and Marwa may simply be omitted.

evidence.title: The questioner’s inference
evidence.text: Urwa makes that inference in the cited report.

evidence.title: Aisha’s answer
evidence.text: Aisha rejects it and explains the earlier hesitation behind the wording.

cases.correction: Read the complete verse with Aisha’s explanation rather than treating the isolated phrase as a complete ruling.
cases.limit: Legal detail and school-specific discussion require more than this short exercise.
cases.skill: A source can preserve a mistaken question without endorsing it.

sources.label: Sahih al-Bukhari 1643
sources.note: Urwa’s question and Aisha’s correction about Safa and Marwa.

passage.arabic: ۞ إِنَّ ٱلصَّفَا وَٱلْمَرْوَةَ مِن شَعَآئِرِ ٱللَّهِ ۖ فَمَنْ حَجَّ ٱلْبَيْتَ أَوِ ٱعْتَمَرَ فَلَا جُنَاحَ عَلَيْهِ أَن يَطَّوَّفَ بِهِمَا ۚ وَمَن تَطَوَّعَ خَيْرًا فَإِنَّ ٱللَّهَ شَاكِرٌ عَلِيمٌ
passage.translation: Lo! (the mountains) As-Safa and Al-Marwah are among the indications of Allah. It is therefore no sin for him who is on pilgrimage to the House (of Allah) or visiteth it, to go around them (as the pagan custom is). And he who doeth good of his own accord, (for him) lo! Allah is Responsive, Aware.

cases.title: Response or cause?
cases.claim: Abu Talha’s offer of his garden caused 3:92 to be revealed.

evidence.title: The sequence
evidence.text: The report places the verse’s revelation before Abu Talha’s offer.

evidence.title: The response
evidence.text: The garden is his response to the teaching he heard.

cases.correction: The cited report describes what happened after revelation, not the garden offer as its cause.
cases.limit: A single account of response does not list every circumstance known about a verse.
cases.skill: Check the direction of the narrative sequence.

sources.label: Sahih al-Bukhari 1461
sources.note: Anas’s report about the beloved garden and charitable giving.

passage.arabic: لَن تَنَالُوا۟ ٱلْبِرَّ حَتَّىٰ تُنفِقُوا۟ مِمَّا تُحِبُّونَ ۚ وَمَا تُنفِقُوا۟ مِن شَىْءٍ فَإِنَّ ٱللَّهَ بِهِۦ عَلِيمٌ
passage.translation: Ye will not attain unto piety until ye spend of that which ye love. And whatsoever ye spend, Allah is Aware thereof.

cases.title: A house is not a tensile-strength claim
cases.claim: 29:41 says spider silk is the weakest material in the world.

evidence.title: The actual image
evidence.text: The verse names a spider’s house, not a laboratory measure of silk.

evidence.title: Retrieved commentary
evidence.text: Al-Muyassar explains the comparison in terms of reliance on protectors besides Allah.

cases.correction: The reading concerns a fragile refuge in a comparison about reliance. It does not present a materials-science ranking.
cases.limit: Do not turn this scope correction into an unsupported claim about the strongest or weakest fiber.
cases.skill: Keep an analogy’s stated subject separate from a modern measurement.

passage.arabic: مَثَلُ ٱلَّذِينَ ٱتَّخَذُوا۟ مِن دُونِ ٱللَّهِ أَوْلِيَآءَ كَمَثَلِ ٱلْعَنكَبُوتِ ٱتَّخَذَتْ بَيْتًا ۖ وَإِنَّ أَوْهَنَ ٱلْبُيُوتِ لَبَيْتُ ٱلْعَنكَبُوتِ ۖ لَوْ كَانُوا۟ يَعْلَمُونَ
passage.translation: The likeness of those who choose other patrons than Allah is as the likeness of the spider when she taketh unto herself a house, and lo! the frailest of all houses is the spider's house, if they but knew.

cases.title: Does ancestry settle honor?
cases.claim: 49:13 names tribes in order to rank human worth by ancestry.

evidence.title: Shared origin
evidence.text: The passage begins with shared human origin.

evidence.title: Its stated distinction
evidence.text: Al-Muyassar explains that ancestry is not the basis of superiority; the passage names taqwa.

cases.correction: The cited reading does not make ancestry a guarantee of honor.
cases.limit: The app does not judge any individual’s taqwa or assign a personal religious rank.
cases.skill: Read the reason and criterion actually stated in the passage.

passage.arabic: يَـٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلنَّاسُ إِنَّا خَلَقْنَـٰكُم مِّن ذَكَرٍ وَأُنثَىٰ وَجَعَلْنَـٰكُمْ شُعُوبًا وَقَبَآئِلَ لِتَعَارَفُوٓا۟ ۚ إِنَّ أَكْرَمَكُمْ عِندَ ٱللَّهِ أَتْقَىٰكُمْ ۚ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ عَلِيمٌ خَبِيرٌ
passage.translation: O mankind! Lo! We have created you male and female, and have made you nations and tribes that ye may know one another. Lo! the noblest of you, in the sight of Allah, is the best in conduct. Lo! Allah is Knower, Aware.

cases.title: Ability to pay and a delay
cases.claim: The cited report says delaying a due debt is harmless when the debtor is wealthy.

evidence.title: The debtor’s ability
evidence.text: The report specifically concerns an able debtor.

evidence.title: Its evaluation
evidence.text: It describes the delay as injustice.

cases.correction: Sahih al-Bukhari 2400 does not excuse avoidable delay by the able debtor.
cases.limit: Do not apply this to genuine inability without checking the different facts and relevant sources.
cases.skill: Do not reverse a source’s condition.

sources.label: Sahih al-Bukhari 2400
sources.note: Abu Hurayra’s report about delay by an able debtor.

cases.title: The habit a report praises
cases.claim: The cited report praises repeated lying as a path to righteousness.

evidence.title: Two habits
evidence.text: The report contrasts truthfulness and falsehood.

evidence.title: Their direction
evidence.text: It connects truthfulness, not repeated lying, with righteousness.

cases.correction: Sahih al-Bukhari 6094 praises truthfulness and warns about lying.
cases.limit: The exercise does not decide the moral state of a named person or resolve every exceptional legal discussion about speech.
cases.skill: Check which verb belongs to which outcome.

sources.label: Sahih al-Bukhari 6094
sources.note: The report links habits of speech with their consequences.

cases.title: Filling a narrator’s blank
cases.claim: The cited 49:2 report identifies both proposed candidates with no uncertainty.

evidence.title: A retained gap
evidence.text: The sub-narrator says he does not remember one name.

evidence.title: The event
evidence.text: The account still describes the disagreement and rising voices.

cases.correction: Preserve the name uncertainty in this report. A detail from another source needs separate attribution.
cases.limit: A gap in one narrator’s memory does not make every other detail of the report unknown.

sources.label: Sahih al-Bukhari 4845
sources.note: Ibn Abi Mulaika’s narration preserves a sub-narrator’s uncertainty.

passage.arabic: يَـٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوا۟ لَا تَرْفَعُوٓا۟ أَصْوَٰتَكُمْ فَوْقَ صَوْتِ ٱلنَّبِىِّ وَلَا تَجْهَرُوا۟ لَهُۥ بِٱلْقَوْلِ كَجَهْرِ بَعْضِكُمْ لِبَعْضٍ أَن تَحْبَطَ أَعْمَـٰلُكُمْ وَأَنتُمْ لَا تَشْعُرُونَ
passage.translation: O ye who believe! Lift not up your voices above the voice of the Prophet, nor shout when speaking to him as ye shout one to another, lest your works be rendered vain while ye perceive not.

cases.title: The order of chapters is not a full event chronology
cases.claim: Because Al-Alaq is chapter 96, the cited first-revelation report puts it near the end of the mission.

evidence.title: What the report describes
evidence.text: Aisha describes the beginning of revelation at Hira with the opening reading instructions.

evidence.title: Different orderings
evidence.text: A chapter’s mushaf number is not an event date supplied by this report.

cases.correction: Use the report’s actual account of the beginning of revelation. A mushaf chapter number does not establish a late event date.
cases.limit: This account concerns the opening verses, not an exact date for every ayah in Al-Alaq.
cases.skill: Distinguish a catalog position from historical sequence.

sources.label: Sahih al-Bukhari 4953
sources.note: Aisha’s report about the beginning of revelation.

passage.arabic:
ٱقْرَأْ بِٱسْمِ رَبِّكَ ٱلَّذِى خَلَقَ
خَلَقَ ٱلْإِنسَـٰنَ مِنْ عَلَقٍ
ٱقْرَأْ وَرَبُّكَ ٱلْأَكْرَمُ
ٱلَّذِى عَلَّمَ بِٱلْقَلَمِ
عَلَّمَ ٱلْإِنسَـٰنَ مَا لَمْ يَعْلَمْ
passage.translation:
Read: In the name of thy Lord Who createth,
Createth man from a clot.
Read: And thy Lord is the Most Bounteous,
Who teacheth by the pen,
Teacheth man that which he knew not.

methodology: Twelve constructed reading claims are checked against fixed, specifically identified sources. They are exercises in misquotation, context, sequence and evidence limits, not a list of measured viral trends or accusations about people. Classifications describe what the cited material supports. “Beyond the cited evidence” does not mean that every other source has been searched or that the broader proposition is false. The app accepts no arbitrary claim for live judgment. Quran readings are canonical, and commentary and hadith notes remain attributed original paraphrases.
